title: Latency-proportional geo pinning with backpressure-aware queueing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe two classes of failures during cross-region load spikes: (1) requests routed to the geographically closest region suffer high p95/p99 latency because the region is CPU/GPU-bound, and (2) global hedging increases downstream load and amplifies queueing in healthy regions, causing cascading tail latency. Current routing uses fixed geo-pinning with ad-hoc fallback; circuit breaker behavior is coarse and often results in hard rejects rather than graceful degradation.

Goal: Implement a latency-proportional weighting router that steers requests across regions based on a combined signal of observed tail latency, usable capacity credits, and recent failure rates. Integrate a backpressure-aware queuing layer at the edge that applies soft circuit-breakers (shed-to-degrade) instead of immediate hard rejects. Design must be rollout-safe, observable, and compatible with Dedicated pools and Private deployments.

Constraints and non-goals: We will not change model selection/quantization behavior in this ticket. This is routing + edge queue behavior only. The feature must be togglable per-customer and default-off for customers in Private mode until RBAC controls are available.

Design summary: Router computes region score = w_latency * inverse_tail_latency_rank + w_capacity * capacity_credit_score + w_errors * (1 - recent_error_rate). We use an exponentially-weighted moving percentile (EWMP) for p95/p99 to smooth spikes. Scores are normalized across active regions and converted to routing probability. Geo pinning is preserved by a pin_strength parameter: probability = pin_strength * locality_indicator + (1 - pin_strength) * probability_from_scores. pin_strength is configurable per-route, default 0.85 for low-latency routes.

Backpressure queue: Each edge gateway maintains a leaky-bucket queue for each downstream region pool. When queue length exceeds soft_threshold, the gateway activates graded degradation: (a) enable prefix-caching (if available) and serve cached completions for eligible requests, (b) shrink request-level max_tokens/response window (for compatible routes), and (c) shift additional proportion of traffic to other regions using a fast ephemeral weight bump. If queue exceeds hard_threshold, gateway emits a 503-like graceful_degrade response that triggers client-side fallback to a lower-quality model. All degrade decisions are logged with reason codes for downstream analysis.

Soft circuit-breaker policy: based on run-rate, error-rate, and queue latency. Breaker moves through states: CLOSED -> SOFT_DEGRADED -> COOLDOWN -> OPEN. Transitions recorded with timestamps and metrics. During SOFT_DEGRADED we route reduced volume and enable degradation steps; during OPEN we avoid routing to the region for a cooldown window but continue to monitor health.

Observability and SLOs: Expose per-route, per-region metrics: routed_qps, queued_count, queue_latency_p50/p95/p99, degrade_rate, fallback_rate, and score_components (latency_score, capacity_score, error_score). SLOs to maintain: global p95 <= configured SLO and fallback_rate < 1% for paid customers. Add alerts: sustained degrade_rate > 1% for 5m, fallback_rate > 0.5% for 3m, and region open_count > 3 in 1h.

Rollout and safety: Feature gated behind runtime-2.4 feature flag and per-customer toggle. Start with canary region and 1% of global traffic, then 5%, 20% if metrics are within thresholds. Automatic rollback if degrade_rate exceeds thresholds or if global p99 increases by >20% over baseline.

Testing: Unit tests for score normalization, EWMP implementation, and state machine of soft circuit-breaker. Integration test harness simulating region overload with synthetic latency and capacity signals. Chaos test: inject sudden node loss in a region and assert no more than 5% of traffic experiences hard errors.

Documentation and runbook links: design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Latency-Proportional+Geo+Pinning, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/18214, dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/geo-routing/latency-proportional-router.
acceptance_criteria: Router computes stable normalized scores and exposes score_components per-region
Backpressure queue enacts graded degradation (cache, response trimming, reroute) before hard rejects
Soft circuit-breaker transitions logged and enforced; open state prevents new routing to region
Canary rollout completed without exceeding degrade or fallback SLOs
Dashboards and alerts created for the new metrics
testing_plan: Unit: EWMP and scoring logic coverage >= 90%
Integration: synthetic latency/capacity tests in staging simulating 3 failure modes
Load: 2h soak at 2x normal QPS with intermittent 30% region node loss
Chaos: terminate 2/3 machines in a regional pool and validate fallback behavior
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated in runtime-2.4; default off
Canary: 1% traffic for 48h with tight alerts
Post-rollout: 7-day observation and automatic rollback trigger for SLO breaches
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Serving, and Console teams. Agreed on pin_strength default and canary plan.
2026-02-18: Prototype EWMP implemented in router; initial unit tests added. Early results show smoother p95 spikes in synthetic traces.
2026-02-26: Design review feedback from SRE: add explicit logging for degrade_reason codes and increase observability granularity to per-route.
2026-03-03: Integration tests in staging revealed a regression where capacity_credit_score did not decay correctly; fixed and added regression test.
2026-03-10: Eng + PM review: approved for canary. Preparing runtime-2.4 branch and feature-flag wiring. Assigned infra change request for edge gateways (INFRA-778).
